brief: The canvas depicts a vast, deep cross-section of horizontally stacked rock layers, rendered in shades of stone, earth, and crystalline metamorphic hues. Over time, the structure visibly and slowly shifts under the relentless force of plate friction. The rock formations continually interact, showing subtle fracturing, gradual uplift, and visible slippage where segments of the strata pass past one another, constructing the massive, mountainous shapes of a forming range.

statement: This sketch depicts a dynamic cross-section of geological strata undergoing tectonic forces. Through subtle wave motions, simulated slippage, and occasional fracturing, the layered rock formations evolve over time to suggest the slow, powerful processes that build mountain ranges. The use of WEBGL rendering allows for a more immersive 3D perspective while maintaining the performance constraints necessary for smooth animation. Viewer interaction is minimal, as the geological drama unfolds autonomously through procedural animation techniques that create an ever-changing landscape of stone and sediment.
